title: Distinct in a Sorted List
statement:
A librarian keeps `ids` sorted from smallest to largest, but some IDs were entered more than once.

Return **how many different IDs** the list contains.

hints.nudge: The list is sorted, so equal IDs sit side by side. When does a new ID begin?
hints.pattern: Compare each element with the previous one (a slow pointer marks the last distinct value).
hints.pseudocode:
count = 1
for i from 1 to n-1: if ids[i] != ids[i-1]: count++
return count
hints.walkthrough: You do not need a set: because the list is sorted, all copies of a value are next to each other. A new distinct value starts exactly where an element differs from the one before it. Count those starts, plus the first element. One pass, O(1) space.
